protections: Download-path confinement: package id/subdir/filename and the zip extraction root come from the index and must resolve inside the caller-chosen download_dir; no such control exists at this pin (nltk/downloader.py:265, :275, :691, :707, :728).

Resource-read confinement: nltk.data.find/_open must not resolve a resource name outside the configured data paths once percent- and backslash-encoded forms are decoded; only a pre-decode os.path.normpath exists (nltk/data.py:237, :242, :507, :531).
Fetch-target restriction: urlopen targets taken from package metadata or from a custom index URL are not scheme- or host-constrained (nltk/downloader.py:706, :949).
Install-time integrity: the downloaded archive is extracted before any checksum comparison; the index-supplied MD5 is consulted only by a later status check (nltk/downloader.py:705-737, :896).

Pre-existing at the pin and not the candidate's missing control: nltk.data.load already restricts pickle classes (nltk/data.py:661-667, :763) and uses yaml.safe_load (:778); the B advisory's nltk.pathsec module and its ENFORCE flag are absent from the entire tree.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The index is project-owned HTTPS metadata and the changelog calls a compromised download server an 'unlikely situation' that was already fixed (ChangeLog:211-213), so an XML attribute such as filename overriding the computed name at nltk/downloader.py:275 reads as trusted stored configuration rather than attacker input.

Deleting a stale package file and creating the install subdirectory look like ordinary pre-transfer cleanup, so a guard placed at the open/write call (nltk/downloader.py:707) appears to cover the operation even though both side effects already consumed the unvalidated path.

normalize_resource_name already runs os.path.normpath (nltk/data.py:237), so a check that normalizes the resource name before joining is believed to have removed '..'; leading '..' survives normpath on relative names, and url2pathname is only applied later at the join (nltk/data.py:531), so percent- and backslash-encoded forms are decoded after that normalization and a normpath-based guard misses them.

file: URLs with absolute paths are documented and doctested behaviour (nltk/data.py:15-16; nltk/test/data.doctest:52-56, :159), so leaving the file: branch at nltk/data.py:885-887 unconfined is intentional rather than a missing control, and a rule that confines it breaks a must-keep-working value.

The default index is the project's HTTPS endpoint (nltk/downloader.py:458) and choosing another index URL is an explicit user action (nltk/downloader.py:52-59), while the package URL is metadata from that same index, so no scheme or host check looks necessary at the fetch site.

The MD5 is taken from the same index as the URL (nltk/downloader.py:245), so it is not an independent trust anchor and verifying it at install time looks redundant; the existing comparison at nltk/downloader.py:896 only runs during a later status check, after the archive has already been extracted at :727-733.

File ids are corpus-internal identifiers selected by the reader, and joining them onto the corpus root is the documented way to reach a corpus file (nltk/corpus/reader/api.py:161-170, :222-232), so they do not look like request-controlled paths and the join at nltk/data.py:332-334 adds no check.

masking: The percent/backslash shape in T3 only defeats the guard once a normalization-based check is added to nltk.data.find; with no guard at the pin every name is accepted, so the shape becomes observable only after the literal '..' route in the same function is fixed.

The downloader traps T1/T2/T5/T6 only become observable once pathsec enforcement is on: while the A-era control is controlled by a default-false switch (the B advisory), every check is a no-op and the sinks behave exactly as they do at this pin.

conflicts.what: A single global pathsec policy that turns enforcement on for both writes and reads (the natural fix for T1, and exactly what the B fix flips) also confines nltk.data reads and rejects the documented absolute file: loads that T4 must keep working (nltk/data.py:15-16; nltk/test/data.doctest:52-56, :159).

Fixing T2 by normalizing and confining the resource name at nltk/data.py:507-531 must still allow absolute file: paths (T3); percent decoding therefore has to happen before the confinement test, and a check that runs on the pre-decode name breaks the T3 must-keep-working value.

fairness_risks: Custom download_dir must remain any caller-chosen writable path, including nested non-existent parents (nltk/downloader.py:46-47, :616-620; nltk/test/unit/test_downloader.py:4-19); a rule that permits writes only under CWD or NLTK's own data directory breaks this legitimate use.

A caller-supplied server_index_url is documented (nltk/downloader.py:52-59, :484-486) and may be a mirror or a local index; forbidding non-GitHub or non-HTTPS index URLs breaks that documented configuration.

Absolute file: resource loads are documented and doctested (nltk/data.py:15-16; nltk/test/data.doctest:52-56, :159), and nltk.data.retrieve writes to a caller-chosen filename relative to CWD (nltk/test/data.doctest:168-179); a blanket 'no reads or writes outside nltk_data' rule contradicts both.

Corpus file ids legitimately contain separators for nested corpus layouts (nltk/corpus/reader/ycoe.py:41-43 joins 'psd' and 'pos' onto the corpus root; nltk/corpus/reader/api.py:170, :195, :231 pass caller file ids straight through), so a rule that refuses any file id containing a separator or a '..' component also refuses shapes legitimate corpus code produces.

design.why: Five independent guards, each with a different dismissal argument, and both model-specific failure modes. The deepseek trio is where a protection is simply absent under a plausible 'trusted configuration' reason: index-supplied destination path (T1, whose remove/mkdir ordering T2 shares and which one validation at the package-record boundary closes), the official-HTTPS index argument for the fetch target (T5), and checksum-from-the-same-index for install integrity (T6); a solver that accepts 'the index is trusted' loses all three. The mimo pair is where the tempting fix is over-broad: T3 shows normalization-before-decode shapes defeating a normpath-style check, and T4 requires keeping documented absolute file: loads while still blocking escapes. The five guards are behaviourally separable (destination path, resource-name decoding, read-root policy, fetch target, install-time integrity), so tests can distinguish partial fixes. T7 (corpus-reader join) is a real but distant second read path and is left out of the five. Caveat for the harness: the B advisory's nltk.pathsec module is not in this checkout, so the stacked task must be scoped to these A-era sinks visible at the pin; if hidden tests import pathsec symbols, the candidate needs re-pinning to the parent of b_fix 155e40343cff.
